51511406.DESCRIPTION: Inhibition of human USP7 using Ub-Rho110 as substrate assessed as dissociation constant by fluorescence based SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed using a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare). The human USP7 catalytic domain (residues 209–560) was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip via amine coupling. The immobilization level was approximately 1000 response units (RU). The running buffer was 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% P20, and 0.01% Tween 20. The analyte, Ub-Rho110, was prepared in the running buffer and injected at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 nM. The association phase lasted 120 seconds, followed by a 120-second dissociation phase. Regeneration was achieved by injecting 10 mM glycine, pH 2.0, for 30 seconds. Data were collected and analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The dissociation constant (Kd) was calculated from the sensorgrams using a 1:1 Langmuir binding model.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Fig. 2. Sensorgrams of Ub-Rho110 binding to immobilized USP7 catalytic domain. The analyte concentrations are indicated in the figure. The association phase is shown in the first 120 seconds, followed by a 120-second dissociation phase. The regeneration step is shown at the end of each cycle. The data were fitted to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model to determine the dissociation constant (Kd).
original_paragraph.Table 1: The IC50 values for USP7 were determined using the Ub-Rho110 assay, which is based on surface plasmon resonance (SPR) technology. The assay measures the inhibition of USP7 activity by monitoring the binding of Ub-Rho110 to the immobilized USP7 catalytic domain. The dissociation constant (Kd) for the interaction between Ub-Rho110 and USP7 was determined to be 0.12 nM. The IC50 values were calculated from the SPR data using a competitive binding model.
original_paragraph.Supporting Information S1: The SPR experiments were conducted as described in the Materials and Methods section. The sensorgrams for the binding of Ub-Rho110 to USP7 at different concentrations are shown in Figure S1. The data were fitted to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model, and the dissociation constant (Kd) was calculated to be 0.12 nM. The IC50 values for the inhibitors were determined by measuring the concentration required to inhibit 50% of the binding of Ub-Rho110 to USP7. The results are summarized in Table S1.
